subjective: Gnocki, a female cat, has had localized hair loss noticed since yesterday. There is no known trauma or wound in the area. The owner has not observed any increased grooming or itching. Appetite is normal with no vomiting. No flea or tick prevention is currently used as there are no signs of scratching or parasites. The cat is vaccinated annually, with the last vaccination about a year ago. The owner reports seasonal shedding but no other cats have been checked for similar issues. There is some tension among the three cats in the household.
objective: Physical examination revealed localized hair loss without wounds, lesions, scaly patches, or skin abnormalities. No signs of infection or parasites were observed. The skin in the affected area appears normal. No dirt or external parasites were noted. No signs of excoriation or abrasion. No systemic signs such as vomiting or decreased appetite were observed.
assessment: Localized, superficial hair loss likely due to self-inflicted trauma possibly from rough tongue or mild irritation. No evidence of wounds, infection, or parasitic infestation. Seasonal shedding may contribute. No signs of dermatophytosis or other skin infections as no lesions or scaling were observed. The condition is currently mild and non-painful.
plan:
Therapeutic: Prescribe a topical ointment to be applied to the affected area for 5 days.
Monitoring: Owner to observe for improvement over 4-5 days.
Diagnostic: If no improvement or worsening occurs, consider skin scraping or sample test to rule out infection or other dermatologic conditions.
Owner Instructions: Avoid use of an Elizabethan collar if possible due to cat's stress and household dynamics; monitor licking behavior closely. Contact clinic if the cat continues to lick the area excessively or if new lesions appear.
Follow-up: Schedule a recheck in 4-5 days to assess response to treatment.
conclusion: Gnocki presented with a recent onset of localized hair loss without wounds or signs of infection. Examination showed normal skin with no lesions or parasites. The hair loss is likely self-inflicted due to mild irritation or rough tongue, possibly exacerbated by seasonal shedding. A topical ointment was prescribed for 5 days with instructions to monitor the area. If the condition does not improve or worsens, further diagnostic testing will be considered. The owner was advised to avoid using a cone due to stress and social tension among the cats but to monitor licking behavior closely. A follow-up appointment is planned in 4-5 days to evaluate progress.
key_issues:
1. Localized hair loss without wounds or infection - likely self-inflicted due to mild irritation or rough tongue.
Remarks: Mild superficial hair loss with normal skin; no immediate concern but requires monitoring.
2. Potential for worsening if licking continues.
Remarks: Owner advised to monitor licking and apply ointment to promote healing.
abnormal_findings: Localized hair loss without skin lesions or wounds.
customer_instructions: Apply the prescribed topical ointment to the affected area for 5 days. Monitor the area for improvement. Avoid using an Elizabethan collar if possible due to the cat's stress and household dynamics. If the cat continues to lick the area excessively or if new lesions appear, contact the clinic promptly. Schedule a recheck in 4-5 days to assess healing.
reminders: Recheck appointment in 4-5 days to evaluate improvement of hair loss and skin condition. Contact clinic earlier if condition worsens or new lesions develop.
